questions.question: In a dual air brake system, what is true?

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system to use.
Only brakes on one side of the vehicle work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: Heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. This means there are two separate brake systems connected to one set of brake controls. Each system has its own air tanks.

questions.question: What should you do with wheel rims that have been welded?

options.text: Put them in the front of the vehicle.
Put them in the rear of the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Welded wheels and rims are not safe. Replace any damaged wheels and rims.

questions.question: When entering traffic, what does a large vehicle usually need?

options.text: Less space than a car needs.
About the same space as a car needs.
More space than a car needs.

questions.correctAnswerText: More space than a car needs.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more space to enter or cross traffic than smaller vehicles. This is because they are bigger and need more distance to speed up.

questions.question: What happens if an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) breaks down?

options.text: A yellow light will turn on in the control panel.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow light will turn on in the control panel.
questions.explanation: When an ABS system breaks down, a yellow warning light will appear on your dashboard to alert you.

questions.question: How should you drive doubles or triples to prevent rolling over?
questions.explanation: To avoid rolling over, drive slowly and steer gently around turns and corners. A safe speed for a single trailer may be too fast for a double or triple trailer.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, where should the trailer height be?

options.text: Slightly higher than the fifth wheel center.
Level with the fifth wheel center.
Slightly lower than the fifth wheel center.
Next to the fifth wheel center.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly lower than the fifth wheel center.
questions.explanation: When connecting a converter dolly, the trailer should be positioned slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.question: What does gravity do when you drive uphill?

options.text: It does not change your speed.
It makes your vehicle swerve left.

questions.explanation: When driving uphill, gravity pulls against your vehicle and slows it down.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Park away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
Call emergency services and tell them where you are.

questions.explanation: Do not pull into a service station during a vehicle fire. The fuel there could catch fire. Instead, drive to an open area away from buildings and vehicles. Call emergency services and report the fire and your location.

questions.question: If you notice an unusual noise or feeling while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Hope the vehicle is okay until someone else drives it.
Check it out to find the problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check it out to find the problem.
questions.explanation: If you see, hear, smell, or feel anything unusual while driving, have it checked right away.

questions.question: At what air pressure level does an air compressor governor stop pumping air?
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping air when the tanks reach 125 psi. This level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: What will happen if brakes are out of adjustment?

options.text: Some brakes will work too hard and fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Some brakes will work too hard and fail.
questions.explanation: Brakes that are out of adjustment will fade faster than properly adjusted brakes. Check your brake adjustment often to prevent brake problems.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Makes it easier to turn a large vehicle.

questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: What is the most common type of foundation brake?
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: What is true about broken suspension parts?

options.text: They should be repaired but can wait.

questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up your vehicle and keeps the axles in place. When checking your vehicle, look for damaged spring hangers, spring leaves, shock absorbers, u-bolts, and frame members. Broken suspension parts are very dangerous.

questions.question: Where are braking mechanisms located?
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are attached to the wheels on the axles. The parts that stop the vehicle are inside the drum brake.

questions.question: Is eating while driving safe?

options.text: Yes, if the food is easy to eat.

questions.explanation: Smoking, eating, or drinking while driving takes your attention away from the road. Plan ahead and stop to eat on long trips.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?

options.text: The brakes may be slow to respond.

questions.explanation: Using the brake pedal too much can let air out faster than the compressor can replace it. If air pressure drops too low, the air brakes may not work.

questions.question: How long does it take for oil pressure to reach normal after starting an engine?
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should reach normal levels within seconds after starting the engine. Do not drive if oil pressure is low, dropping, or changing.

questions.question: What should you do when it is hard to see other vehicles at dawn or dusk?
questions.explanation: At dawn, dusk, or in bad weather, use your headlights on low beam to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What should a driver do if a tire fails?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel with one hand and wave with the other.

questions.explanation: Using the brakes when a tire fails can cause you to lose control. Stay off the brakes unless you must avoid something dangerous. Once your vehicle slows down, brake very gently, move off the road, and stop.
